jina.title: How to Launch on Product Hunt (And What to Realistically Expect)
jina.snippet:
For many first-time founders, a Product Hunt launch feels like the official birthday of their product. You see the stories: a maker posts at midnight, climbs to the top of the day, and wakes up to thousands of visitors and a flood of signups. So one of the first questions after building something is how to launch on Product Hunt and win.

The honest answer starts with a different question: should you launch there at all, and what are you hoping to get? Product Hunt can deliver a burst of attention, useful feedback, a badge for your site, and a few early fans. It rarely delivers a business on its own, and for some apps it barely moves the needle. This guide helps you decide, prepare properly if you go ahead, and get lasting value from one busy day.

## What Product Hunt is good for, and what it is not

Product Hunt is a daily list of new products, voted on and discussed by a community that skews toward founders, developers, designers, marketers, and early adopters of tools. Launches go live at the start of the day, Pacific time, and compete for attention over the following 24 hours. Product Hunt's team also chooses which launches to feature, and featured launches get far more visibility than those that are not.

**It tends to work well for** productivity tools, AI products, developer and design tools, creator tools, and anything the tech community enjoys trying. These audiences are curious, vocal, and willing to sign up for something new.

**It tends to work less well for** niche consumer apps whose ideal users are not on Product Hunt. A meal planning app for busy parents or a habit app for nurses may get polite upvotes from founders who will never use it. The traffic is real, but the fit is weak.

What our latest launch revealed about who gets seen and whose votes count
Product Hunt's leaderboard is not a level playing field. The team chooses which launches get the homepage. Votes carry different weights. And the products we compared began around 50 points while we began at zero. Those are the displayed starting balances in our screenshots; the dashboard does not establish how they were assigned.
On November 10, we launched Sell Personal Agents with Pickaxe. We estimate that around 150 people upvoted us. We finished with 42 points, in position #52. The starting balance of the top three launches in our dashboard was larger than everything we earned all day.
We also gained more points after launch than four products in our dashboard comparison, yet stayed buried below page one. A final ranking leaves out a lot when it puts editorial selection, unequal starting positions, and weighted votes behind a single number.
Product Hunt chooses who gets seen
Product Hunt hand-picks the launches that appear on its homepage leaderboard. Its own explanation of how the platform works says that featured launches compete for the day's ranking, including Product of the Day. Editorial selection determines who enters that competition.
The AMA with Gabe Perez, who leads leaderboard curation, states it directly in the title: “I decide what's featured on the leaderboard.”
If you aren't selected, your launch still goes live, but it sits outside the default homepage feed.
